# AGENTS.md — Enterprise Linux Audit Policy v0.19

**Current release:** v0.19 (engineering candidate). The current source of truth is the GitHub `main` rule tree and four guides in `docs/` (01–04). Historical release references below are milestones, not current version claims.

## v0.18 historical SSH decisions and v0.19 configuration-monitoring update

- **OpenSSH:** v0.18 activated targeted `/etc/ssh` subtree watches in Ubuntu and RHEL 9 profiles. v0.19 now adds broad `/etc` auditd coverage across all 80 variants, including SSH config changes where the directory exists or is newly created. Keep existing targeted selectors for traceability; some legacy exact-path rules remain conditional.
- **Sudoers:** existing Tier 1/2 sudoers watches remain unchanged. v0.19 `/etc` directory auditing now covers sudoers creation/modification when sudo is installed even if target files were absent at rule load; commented exact-path candidates do not count as active.
- **Loader preload first creation:** v0.19 approves and activates the recursive `dir=/etc` watch for this missing-file scenario. No additional endpoint collector is assumed. Flag the broad-watch volume/overlap risk without silently deactivating it.
- **Magic SysRq:** the `kernel.sysrq` sysctl affects keyboard use; privileged writes to `/proc/sysrq-trigger` remain available. Procfs candidates stay disabled until target-kernel audit acceptance is confirmed. Do not conflate sysctl configuration with trigger attribution.
- **Settled `-f 2`:** remains the one mandatory Tier 1 fail-secure directive in `18-security-critical.rules` per profile; do not change except via approved waiver. Final `-e 2` remains separate.
- **Current change scope:** v0.19 adds 120 `t2_etc_integrity` directives in all 80 variants. The 48 SSH additions occurred in v0.18. No previous active rule directives were removed or modified. Existing cloud-root-scoped `/etc` rules remain separate.
- **Validation status:** static only; no production/host certification. Preserve exact paths, architecture and applicability conditions.

# AGENTS.md — Enterprise Linux Audit Policy

## v0.19 approved design decision — auditd is the required host source

**Settled requirement:** Tier 1/2 Linux host monitoring must stand on `auditd`. Do not introduce a supplementary host sensor as a mandatory dependency or suggested workaround for baseline gaps. Auditd is the source; Splunk may ingest its events. External cloud provider control-plane records are a distinct technical boundary, not host auditd capabilities.

**Approved Tier 2 addition:** Every variant now actively watches writes and attributes recursively under `/etc` using `-F dir=/etc -F perm=wa -k t2_etc_integrity` (x86_64 b64+b32, ARM64 b64); 120 active directives in 80 variants. This captures initial creation and modification of loader preload files and changes to SSH/sudoers configurations under `/etc` without assuming optional leaf files exist. Existing targeted watches and audit keys are retained. **This is a broad, intentional policy decision, not an unapproved candidate.** Measure/assess volume, overlap and backlog before rollout; maintain `-f 2` and use a formal waiver when unsupported. Do not reopen based solely on broadness without new evidence of a concrete issue.

**Magic SysRq:** `/etc/sysctl*` configuration modifications fall under the `/etc` rule. Direct writes to `/proc/sysrq-trigger` are not proven by it, and procfs candidates stay commented until kernel-specific acceptance testing. This is a known auditd-only limitation, not permission to demand an auxiliary endpoint agent.

**Prior false-positive closure:** The former commented loader *leaf* candidate in `29-system-config-integrity.rules` is superseded/removed. The actual active rule is **directory-wide**; do not count mentions of a filename in prose as duplicate active rules. The old v0.16.3 single-commented-candidate finding is historical, not the current implementation.

> **Purpose:** Portable handoff instructions for AI coding/review agents working on this Linux `auditd` policy project. Read this file, the current `README.md`, and all four guides under `docs/` before changing rules. Treat statements here as project decisions, **not** proof that an individual host or STIG requirement is compliant.

All 49 published audit-rule-related V-IDs are mapped to active directives in the eight Ubuntu 22.04 implementations. The exact 49-row table is in `docs/03-RULE-SOURCING-AND-MAINTENANCE.md`. This **closes the missing audit-rule-ID inventory gap**, but **does not** close official DISA ZIP/XCCDF hash verification, conditional image path/package prerequisites, kernel loading, or actual STIG compliance. Do not reopen the "missing 49 audit-rule IDs" issue without naming a specific V-ID and demonstrating a missing or semantically invalid *active* directive. Continue reporting legitimate unverified deployment and official-source checks. Tier 2 `29-system-config-integrity.rules` has active system shell startup watches and a **v0.19 approved active recursive `/etc` integrity watch**; the obsolete loader leaf candidate was removed.


## Historical v0.17 Tier 2 integrity decision — targeted shell watches

**Historical decision at v0.17:** CVE-independent modifications to system shell initialization were mandatory Tier 2; the broad `/etc` proposal was then inactive and was activated in v0.19. Each implementation now contains active watches under `29-system-config-integrity.rules` for `/etc/profile`, its platform Bash initialization path (`/etc/bashrc` on RHEL-family/Amazon, `/etc/bash.bashrc` on Ubuntu/Debian/SLES) and `/etc/profile.d` for non-Debian profiles. Debian's `profile.d` watch remains commented because base-files does not guarantee it. No per-user home dotfile watches were activated. Exactly **348 active rules added** across the 80 variants; otherwise active directives unchanged from v0.16.4.

**Historical v0.17 decision:** the loader leaf watch was a single commented candidate and no broad `/etc` watch was activated *at that release*; v0.19 supersedes this with active broad directory coverage. SysRq procfs candidates remain inactive. SSH/sudoers watches are already active in some Tier 1 profiles, but others still need package-specific validation. Never claim all these objectives are complete merely because the shell-init watches are active. The settled `-f 2` placement/policy and separate CVE-named Tier 3 files remain unchanged.

**Path evidence:** Default directory or binary paths are supported by published vendor docs/package manifests, *not* proven present on every golden/minimal image. `path=` and `dir=` watches require an existing target; check package/image inventories and handle N/A/waiver as prescribed. No host logs or kernel-loading evidence are available.

## 1. Project objective and boundaries

Produce a comprehensive, maintainable enterprise **Linux Audit Policy** for on-premises and cloud-hosted Linux systems. It must support:

- Applicable OS/version/architecture STIG or authorized SRG audit requirements.
- Consistent, useful SOC detection and incident-response telemetry (Splunk Enterprise Security / risk-based alerting).
- Independently selectable, **CVE-named** exploit-detection rules for assets pending patching or needing targeted monitoring.
- Straightforward deployment by selecting the **exact hosting environment, OS release, and CPU architecture**. The delivered profile must not require customers to assemble generic overlays.
- Source traceability, default-path/package prerequisites, exceptions and periodic maintenance.

**Do not** add deployment scripts, generators, standalone compliance catalogs, combined `.rules` outputs, extra policies, or new documentation types unless specifically asked. The current repository contains the rule tree, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and four guides (01–04). Do not introduce additional deliverables without approval. `AGENTS.md` is a development handoff; it does not impose additional host-side telemetry.

**Do not** assume that a path present in a package repository exists on a given minimal, golden, cloud or customized image. **No real-host testing is available in this workflow**. Report offline findings accurately and leave host-dependent claims unverified.

## 2. Source of truth, layout, and inventory

Use the **latest GitHub repository snapshot**, not an older ZIP or assistant description, as source of truth. The earlier v0.19 ZIP contained **2,000 `.rules` files** and **4 non-rule files** (README + three guides). Current GitHub main adds `docs/04` and `AGENTS.md` (2,006 total files). It has **40 OS/hosting combinations**, **80 architecture-selectable implementations** and **25 `.rules` files per implementation**.

```text
enterprise_audit_policy/
├── README.md
├── docs/
│   ├── 01-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md
│   ├── 02-MINIMUM-SECURITY-REQUIREMENT-AND-WAIVER.md
│   ├── 03-RULE-SOURCING-AND-MAINTENANCE.md
│   └── 04-TIER-2-AND-3-RULE-REFERENCE.md
└── rules/
    ├── on-prem/<os-version>/
    ├── aws/<os-version>/
    ├── azure/<os-version>/
    └── gcp/<os-version>/
```

- **x86_64**: rules in the **immediate** tier directories of `rules/<environment>/<os-version>/`.
- **ARM64 (`aarch64`)**: a separate, complete implementation in the nested `rules/<environment>/<os-version>/aarch64/`.
- Both architecture choices contain their own `tier-1-baseline/`, `tier-2-core-security/`, `tier-3-threat-specific/`, and `finalize/`.
- **Never recursively install a profile directory**, because that would combine mutually exclusive x86_64 and ARM64 sets. Never combine different OS or cloud profiles.
- **Count interpretation:** 25 rule files per implementation includes **comment-only candidates**: 196 of 2,000 files are comment-only (160 PHP2Shell CVE files, 28 on-prem cloud-host stubs, eight conditional MAC-policy files). In v0.16.x the count was 276 before activating 80 Tier 2 `29-system-config-integrity.rules` files. File count does not indicate active sensor coverage.

## 3. Non-negotiable tier policy

| Tier | Purpose | Deployment policy |
|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1 — Baseline** | Audit foundation and all **applicable** OS/version STIG/SRG audit requirements, identity, authentication, privilege, filesystem, MAC controls | **Mandatory** |
| **Tier 2 — Security Monitoring & IR** | CVE-independent SOC/IR monitoring: execution, credentials, persistence, security config, network and relevant cloud-host activity | **Mandatory**, with authorized waivers for justified inability to comply |
| **Tier 3 — Threat Specific** | CVE exploitation sensors, targeted investigations, specialized workload or hunt telemetry | **Select only when applicable or directed**; not a universal install |
| **Finalize** | Apply final audit configuration, including `-e 2` | **Last**, only after authorized preflight/loading decisions |

Minimum Security Requirement (MSR): **Tier 1 + Tier 2**. No unilateral reduction of the MSR. When a valid requirement cannot be supported, document the prerequisite, explicit N/A determination or approved **time-limited waiver**; applicable DoD STIG exceptions require the separate authorized compliance/AO process. Do not equate an enterprise waiver with a STIG waiver.

Preserve intentional `-D` (rule reset), **`-f 2`** (fail-secure; may panic), and **`-e 2`** (immutable until reboot) unless the user explicitly authorizes a policy change. A local or homelab preference for `-f 1` is **not** permission to change all profiles. Account for existing local or vendor audit rules that `-D` may clear.

## 3A. Audit failure mode (`-f 2`) — settled baseline policy; do not re-litigate

**Decision:** The enterprise baseline intentionally uses **`-f 2`** (audit failure mode: panic) in **Tier 1**. This is an accepted *policy design choice with an availability consequence*, **not an overlooked misplaced rule, an unaddressed audit finding, or an automatic request to change it to `-f 1`**. The purpose is fail-secure handling of critical audit failures where the approved baseline requires it. This is distinct from a claim that the risk is suitable for every workload without an applicability/approval review.

**Canonical location and order (v0.16.2):**

- `tier-1-baseline/00-audit-foundation.rules` contains `-D`, `-b 8192`, and `--backlog_wait_time 60000`, plus a **comment** directing maintainers to the failure mode.
- `tier-1-baseline/18-security-critical.rules` contains the single active **`-f 2`** directive for the selected profile, alongside `--loginuid-immutable`. **It is not a Tier 2 rule.**
- `finalize/99-finalize.rules` contains `-e 2` and must be applied last. **`-f 2` and `-e 2` are different controls** and must never be conflated.
- Do not move, duplicate, remove, downgrade, or silently override `-f 2` when doing routine cleanup, STIG mapping, OS-specific work, or responding to repeated third-party review comments. Keep its Tier 1 location and foundation cross-reference unless explicitly instructed to change the enterprise policy.

**Risk and exception handling:** `-f 2` can trigger a kernel panic on critical audit failures, so host availability, backlog/queue pressure, and audit-path reliability are important deployment considerations. A proposed **`-f 1`** setting (log warnings rather than panic) for a homelab, appliance, cloud image, or availability-sensitive workload is **a deviation requiring explicit, scoped approval** under the existing waiver/exception process, not a default replacement. Do not infer that an enterprise waiver alone satisfies a separate DoD STIG/AO exception requirement. State the operational impact plainly; never call `-f 2` harmless or assume performance and failure behavior were host-tested.

**Review rule:** If another reviewer repeatedly flags `-f 2` merely because it can panic, or because it is in `18-security-critical.rules` rather than `00-audit-foundation.rules`, mark it **“acknowledged, intentional Tier 1 baseline control; availability risk documented; no change authorized.”** Escalate only if the reviewer supplies a *new* specific STIG conflict, incorrect effective configuration, deployment-order defect, or an authorized waiver request. Check for exactly **one active `-f 2` per selected architecture profile**, with no unintended `-f` override later in the rule-loading order.

## 4. Tier 3 CVE naming and selection: settled decision

Every **CVE-specific** ruleset must be named **`CVE-YYYY-NNNN.rules`** (allow longer CVE number segments, e.g. `CVE-2026-109618.rules`). Each file must be independently intelligible: CVE identifier, rationale, source/detection reference, applicable OS/kernel/workload, active vs commented rules, prerequisite paths, audit keys, and how to select/retire it.

**v0.16 CVE files (each appears in all 80 variants):**

| File | Intended collection |
|---|---|
| `CVE-2026-31431.rules` | Copy Fail — AF_ALG, `splice`, execution correlation |
| `CVE-2026-43284.rules` | Dirty Frag — `splice`/`vmsplice`, execution correlation |
| `CVE-2026-43500.rules` | Dirty Frag — equivalent sensor requirement |
| `CVE-2026-74580.rules` | Failed raw-socket activity |
| `CVE-2026-109618.rules` | PHP2Shell — workload-specific application/web worker execution |
| `CVE-2026-109619.rules` | PHP2Shell — equivalent workload sensor requirement |

The general `30-exploitation.rules` remains Tier 3 and **is not renamed after a CVE**. The old generic `31-cve.rules` was removed in v0.16. Do **not** misidentify **CVE-2026-111497** as Dirty Frag: it concerns Brotli, not the kernel `splice` behavior.

**Duplicates are allowed across different CVE files** for independent asset selection, but **do not deploy duplicate equivalent rules indiscriminately**. Select one sensor implementation for shared conditions (and track all relevant CVEs), check overlap with Tier 1/2, and preserve audit keys expected by Splunk or explicitly adapt the detections. The keys `af_alg`, `splice_user`, `process_creation`, and `sock_raw_eafnosupport` are important to published examples.

**Do not state that audit rules patch a CVE.** Vendor patches or approved mitigations are the primary response; Tier 3 adds detection or interim visibility. A rule may be commented and not functional until image/workload details are supplied. The PHP2Shell service-executable candidates are **commented out in v0.16**; do not imply they are active.

## 5. CVE-agnostic Tier 2 vs hunt/Tier 3: prior decisions

**Decision standard:** Promote telemetry to Tier 2 only when it meets an **independent, enduring, broadly applicable security requirement**, and the scope/volume is defensible. A Splunk detection that appears in a CVE analytic story **does not itself justify fleet-wide auditd collection**.

| Capability | Policy decision / current status |
|---|---|
| User and root process execution | **Keep in Tier 2**; existing `execve`/`execveat` rules |
| Broad `auid=unset` / non-root service-account execution | **Not automatically Tier 2**; specifically identified through PHP2Shell; use **scoped Tier 3** if independently justified |
| `/etc/ld.so.preload` and system-wide shell config modification | **Tier 2 objective**; v0.17 activated shell watches and v0.19 adds active `/etc` subtree monitoring for missing-loader-file creation |
| SSH, sudoers, sensitive security config modification | Tier 1/2 objective; check existing coverage and avoid needless duplicates |
| Magic SysRq modifications | Tier 2 **candidate**; kernel/path applicability unverified |
| All users' `.bashrc`/`.profile` modifications | Tier 3 / targeted hunt, not fleet-wide baseline |
| Sudoers **read** access | Tier 3 / targeted hunt, not mandatory baseline |
| CVE-specific socket/syscall sequences, service shell behavior | Tier 3 |
| Audit event parsing and field correlation in Splunk | Mandatory **integration requirement**, not necessarily another kernel audit rule |

`29-system-config-integrity.rules` originated in v0.16 as an inactive proposal, with conditional SysRq and leaf-path alternatives. In v0.17, only shell-startup watches were active. **v0.19 has approved and activated the broad `/etc` watch in every variant**; SysRq procfs candidates stay inactive, and the loader leaf candidate was removed as redundant. The duplicated **commented** `/etc/ld.so.preload` candidate block was removed in v0.16.1; the remaining candidate was removed in v0.19 after activating the broad parent watch.

### Resolved review finding — repeated `/etc/ld.so.preload` text is NOT duplicate collection

**Settled disposition (v0.16.3):** The old finding that `29-system-config-integrity.rules` contained four references to the loader preload file was **a comment-text false positive**, not duplicate rules. In v0.16.2 the path appeared on four lines (explanation plus one `# -a ...` candidate), with **zero active directives**. In v0.16.3 all 80 copies were cleaned up so that the literal path appears **exactly once**, in the single commented-out leaf-path proposal. The broad directory integrity candidate is also commented out. This cleanup **did not enable any rules**.

**Required review method:** Strip or ignore lines beginning with `#` when counting active directives and examine candidates separately. Do not infer duplication from a substring count. For v0.19 `29-system-config-integrity.rules`, expect the active `t2_etc_integrity` directory rule (two ABI rules on x86_64, one on ARM64), in addition to the previously active targeted shell rules. No preload leaf rule is active.

**Current v0.19 decision:** broad Tier 2 `/etc` monitoring is explicitly approved and active, with its performance/availability risk documented. The prior false-positive on duplicated loader candidate comments remains closed; do not confuse it with the new actual directory rule.

**Next substantive work:** evaluate image-specific path assumptions for existing STIG watches, workload performance/volume for the approved `/etc` rule, and conditional SysRq procfs acceptance; then Tier 3 hunt candidates separately.

## 6. OS, architecture and cloud specifics

- **Ubuntu 22.04:** Tier 1 expanded; `apparmor_parser` `/sbin` candidate and V2R10 mapping; 49/49 published rule-bearing V-IDs mapped in v0.16.4; independent official archive hash verification and host/load validation **not completed**. V-ID corrections include `useradd` V-288815, cron V-274862, finalizer V-288816. Do not claim STIG certification.
- **Ubuntu 24.04:** user-supplied V1R7 extraction: **64 source directives represented** on x86_64; does not prove live loading, exact independent current-STIG compliance or ARM64 equivalence. Some watch paths require prerequisites, notably `/var/log/sudo.log`; `/sbin/unix_update` may require checking `/usr`-merge alias.
- **Ubuntu 26.04:** inherits Ubuntu 24.04 **engineering objectives**, not 24.04 STIG authority; uses `/usr/sbin/apparmor_parser`. Check released package/image paths and new STIG applicability separately.
- **RHEL 9:** older local V2R10 reference included **81 directives**, not an independent comparison with the currently authoritative DISA publication.
- **Debian 12/13:** coverage expanded but **does not have full active Ubuntu rule-family parity**; optional `sudo`, SSH, PAM, `acl`, AppArmor, cron, and log-file paths are conditional. For **Proxmox VE**, `/etc/pve` is `pmxcfs`/FUSE: do not presume normal audit file watches establish its configuration history. Proxmox cluster FUSE activity is outside the scope of ordinary local auditd file-watch guarantees; document the gap.
- **Amazon Linux 2023 / 2027:** distinct AWS profiles. AL2027 was a **preview-only candidate** at the previous release review; verify current support/GA status before subsequent claims. Standard/minimal AMIs have different installed packages and SSM availability.
- **SELinux vs AppArmor:** use the applicable OS-native MAC implementation. Policy-modification auditing is separate from MAC enforcement and from AVC/denial record ingestion.
- **Architecture:** x86_64 uses b64 and where appropriate b32 compatibility ABI; ARM64 uses native b64 names, including `*at` variants where legacy syscalls are absent. Correct syscall name mapping does **not** prove identical filter semantics or STIG equivalence.
- **Cloud guests:** use provider **and OS** profile; generic noninteractive root activity does not replace exact SSM/Azure/Linux Agent/Google guest-agent watches. Those path-dependent rules are often commented pending installed-package/image verification.
- **Cloud control plane:** mandatory companion sources: **AWS CloudTrail**, **Azure Activity Log**, **GCP Cloud Audit Logs** for API, role/IAM, security-group/NSG/firewall and resource modifications; network flow logs when applicable. `auditd` cannot reconstruct remote provider API changes reliably. Cloud CLI execution != API audit trail.
- **Host-source policy:** auditd is mandatory and self-contained for required host monitoring. Do not specify a separate endpoint agent as a baseline dependency. Some cloud/API operations are technically outside local host auditd.

## 7. Offline verification — required when making a change

We **cannot assume access to actual hosts or their logs**. Use official vendor STIGs, current package file inventories, cloud-image package manifests and documentation, distro package repositories, and ABI syscall tables. Record date, exact OS/version/architecture/image build, URL, content version/hash if available, and confidence. A repository file list proves where **a package** installs files; an image manifest supports whether a package ships on **that image build**; neither proves a runtime-created file exists.

Before distributing an update:

1. **Identify the exact scope and diff.** Compare against the latest ZIP; make only requested changes. Preserve unaffected active directives and all existing tiers.
2. **Map compliance claims.** For each STIG-derived requirement, record current product/version, V-ID, requirement, mapped rule, and whether it is active/conditional/missing/N/A. Prefer official DISA XCCDF/check text, not a copied STIG from an adjacent OS.
3. **Validate paths.** Inspect active `-w`, `-F path=`, `-F dir=` targets. Document package ownership, symlinks, optional agent paths, missing-by-default log files and approved prerequisite or waiver. Never silently remove a required watch.
4. **Check semantics.** Audit filters (`auid`, `uid`, `euid`, `success`, `exit`, `a0`...), syscall/arch interpretation, paths and recursive directory rules, relevant record types, parent-child limitations, and overlaps. Exact duplicate checks alone are insufficient.
5. **Check all profiles and ABIs.** Verify `b64`/`b32` names against appropriate x86_64/i386/AArch64 tables, do not copy b32 onto ARM64, confirm every profile has the same intended file inventory, and that Finalize is separate and last.
6. **Check keys and detection dependencies.** Do not silently rename Splunk-referenced keys. Identify whether needed `SYSCALL`, `EXECVE`, `PROCTITLE`, `PATH`, `CWD`, and event serial fields will be available and correctly parsed; their end-to-end presence **cannot be proven offline**.
7. **Assess deployment risk.** `-D`, `-f 2`, `-e 2`, missing paths, kernel syscall support, and broad `execve`, `connect`, or `dir=/etc` collection can impact system availability/throughput. Do not invent EPS or CPU performance measurements.
8. **Verify package quality.** ZIP test, rule counts, no unintended duplicates/changes, actual active vs commented directives, changelog and README claims, version headers, three docs, and scoped release report. Never mark a profile production-approved on static evidence alone.

**Known evidence limitations:** Ubuntu 24.04 matches supplied review-derived directives; Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9 and most other OS profiles still need independent up-to-date product-specific STIG reconciliation. No live kernel loading, event generation, audit loss/backlog, performance or Splunk forwarding validation has been performed for the 80 variants.

## 9. Editing and communication contract for another AI

- **Do not modify files unless explicitly asked.** An assessment/review request means assessment only.
- Preserve this package's **three tiers + Finalize** and OS/provider/architecture directories. Do not collapse into common files or add mandatory new tooling.
- When asked to implement changes, state **exactly which active directives change**, which are merely comments/candidates, and which profiles are affected. Distinguish CVE threat sensors from CVE-independent SOC baseline requirements.
- **Do not fabricate STIG mapping, source hashes, CVE associations, host test results, install paths, or release approval.** Cite precise sources and note uncertainty.
- Keep the three existing docs and README in sync. **Release housekeeping completed in v0.16.1:** all 2,000 `.rules` files carry consistent v0.16.1 release metadata; 28 RHEL 9 ARM64 baseline headers are normalized; all three guide titles are current; duplicate commented preload candidates are removed; foundation comments reference the unchanged `-f 2` setting in `18-security-critical.rules`. Historical release-language remains in the README where it describes earlier work.
- **v0.16.2 follow-up:** Standardized first-line headers in the 560 Tier 2 proposal and CVE files that retained prose first lines in v0.16.1. No active directives changed.
- Previous review reports and CSV matrices may be provided as supporting evidence, but the most recent **verified ZIP** is canonical for actual active rules.
- Validate created artifacts exist before giving download paths. Prefer small, transparent diffs and a concise validation summary. If you cannot prove something without a host, label it **offline candidate / requires host validation**, not approved.

## 9A. v0.16.2 formatting-only status

- The **560** previously nonstandard first-line headers (**80** inactive `29-system-config-integrity.rules` proposals and **480** CVE-specific files) now start with the same `# TARGET ARCHITECTURE:` header format as the other rule files. Existing CVE rationale, scope, inactive/active state, audit keys, and associated comments are preserved.
- Release labels are updated to `v0.16.2` across all 2,000 rule files; the README and three guide titles are synchronized. **No active audit directives changed from v0.16.1.**
- The established `-f 2` settled policy remains unchanged; exactly one active `-f 2` and one `-e 2` remain in each of the 80 variants.

# Enterprise Linux Audit Policy — v0.19

**Status: ENGINEERING CANDIDATE — no profile is certified STIG-compliant or production-approved by this release.**

## Current repository documentation update (v0.19 rules unchanged)

- Added `docs/04-TIER-2-AND-3-RULE-REFERENCE.md` to explain the intent of Tier 2 and Tier 3 rule files. It is a **non-normative reference**: the selected OS/cloud/architecture `.rules` files determine actual active coverage, and Tier 1 authority remains the applicable STIG/SRG.
- All **1,360 Tier 2/3 rule files** include the `# See docs/04-TIER-2-AND-3-RULE-REFERENCE.md for rule purposes` comment after their header block. The reference comment does not activate, disable, or alter an audit directive.
- The repository now contains **four guides in `docs/`**, plus this README and `AGENTS.md`: **2,006 tracked files**, including **2,000 `.rules` files**. It still has 40 OS/environment combinations and 80 mutually exclusive architecture selections.
- The new reference includes representative examples and architecture-dependent counts, **not** an assertion that every OS uses the same executable paths, active watches, or CVE selection. For implementation, use the exact selected profile and preflight path requirements.


The package retains the v0.14 remediation of several *static* defects identified in the independent v0.11 validation report. **It does not close the remaining platform STIG-reconciliation, file-existence, optional cloud-agent package prerequisites, on-host event-generation, performance, or SIEM-validation gates.**


## v0.19 — Auditd-only host integrity baseline

- **Auditd is the sole mandatory host monitoring dependency.** No secondary endpoint monitoring software is required or specified to meet Tier 1/2 host-rule objectives.
- Activated a **recursive `/etc` write/attribute audit rule** in all 80 architecture variants of `tier-2-core-security/29-system-config-integrity.rules`: x86_64 adds `arch=b64` and `arch=b32`; ARM64 adds `arch=b64`. **120 new active directives**; existing active directives are preserved.
- The directory rule observes creation or modification of loader preload configuration even when the file did not exist at rule-load time. It also monitors SSH/sudoers changes regardless of whether their individual files exist when audit rules load; native `PATH` records are required to determine which file changed.
- Existing Tier 1/2 targeted SSH, sudoers, PAM and shell watches remain in place for their audit keys and compliance provenance. Overlap and extra audit volume must be assessed; do not assert performance acceptance from offline analysis. `-f 2` and `-e 2` are unchanged.
- **Magic SysRq:** persistent `/etc/sysctl*` file modifications are monitored; direct writes to procfs SysRq trigger/control paths are **not certified** from this ZIP. Their conditional `auditd` candidates remain commented until kernel-specific validation. A configuration watch does not demonstrate trigger attribution.
- **Cloud limit:** host auditd cannot observe remotely initiated cloud API, security-group, or IAM changes; any separate cloud control-plane requirements remain outside what an `auditd` ruleset can provide.
- README, all three existing guides, AGENTS.md and 2,000 rule headers updated. Engineering candidate, not host-tested or STIG-certified. Performance, file path, mount-point and kernel acceptance constraints remain applicable.

## v0.18 — Historical: SSH integrity expansion and source-selection decision

- **Activated targeted Tier 2 OpenSSH configuration subtree monitoring** (`-F dir=/etc/ssh -F perm=wa -k t2_ssh_change`) for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04 and RHEL 9 profiles in every available hosting environment: **16 OS/environment combinations × 2 architectures = 32 profile variants; 48 new active directives** (x86_64 b64+b32, ARM64 b64). The directory and package must exist on the deployed image. Other 48 variants remain conditional; applicability must be documented and enabled when OpenSSH is installed.
- **Sudoers:** The existing 32 profiles with active watches are unchanged. In the other 48, the watches are *conditional on sudo installation*; they are not silently considered covered. No blanket watches were activated that could reference missing files.
- **Loader preload:** First-time creation of a normally absent file is **not** captured by the inactive leaf watch. An unfiltered `/etc` recursive watch was *not* promoted to the mandatory Tier 2 baseline. Existing cloud-host rules include a narrower `auid=unset,euid=0,dir=/etc` sensor, which can observe only a subset of loader-related changes. At that release the issue was still open; **v0.19 supersedes that recommendation with active auditd-only `/etc` coverage.**
- **Magic SysRq:** `/proc/sys/kernel/sysrq` and `/proc/sysrq-trigger` serve different functions; `kernel.sysrq` does not block privileged use of `sysrq-trigger`. Kernel/procfs audit watch candidates remain disabled pending platform validation. Do not infer live-control coverage from persistent sysctl configuration watches.
- **Documentation and AGENTS.md:** corrected the stale handoff package reference and updated all guide titles. All existing active rules, all CVE-specific Tier 3 rules, and the settled `-f 2`/`-e 2` controls are preserved.
- **Validation:** Static comparison against v0.17 finds exactly 48 new active directives in 32 profiles, zero removed/modified active directives, and no additional directory-wide `/etc` rules (existing filtered cloud-host watches are unchanged). No host tests, production approval, or current-STIG re-certification is implied.

## v0.17 — Historical: targeted Tier 2 system startup integrity

- Add `/etc/profile.d` subtree monitoring for RHEL-derived/Amazon/Oracle/Rocky/Alma, Ubuntu and SLES where vendor documentation supports it. On **Debian 12/13**, `/etc/profile.d` is **commented/conditional**, because Debian base-files does not guarantee that directory or its sourcing in `/etc/profile`.
- x86_64 variants include both `b64` and `b32` file-watch rules; ARM64 uses native `b64` only. **348 active audit directives added** across 80 variants. All previous active directives, keys, STIG watches, `-f 2`, `-e 2`, and CVE-specific Tier 3 files are preserved.
- **No broad `/etc` recursive watch was activated in v0.17 (superseded in v0.19).** The leaf-path candidate was inactive at that release because a missing file could not be watched. **v0.19 supersedes it with active parent-directory monitoring.**

Previous release notes below record the historical v0.16.x count of 276 before the 80 Tier 2 proposal files acquired active watches.
- Release state remains **engineering candidate**. Standard vendor paths do not guarantee presence on every minimal/custom image. No host-load, event generation, EPS, or Splunk collection validation was performed.

## v0.16: CVE-specific Tier 3 + CVE-independent Tier 2 integrity

- Replaced `31-cve.rules` with **six separately named, threat-directed files** per architecture/profile: `CVE-2026-31431.rules` (Copy Fail), `CVE-2026-43284.rules` and `CVE-2026-43500.rules` (Dirty Frag), `CVE-2026-74580.rules` (failed SOCK_RAW), and `CVE-2026-109618.rules` / `CVE-2026-109619.rules` (PHP2Shell). Generic `30-exploitation.rules` is unchanged.
- **Tier 3 is not an automatic install.** Select ONLY CVE files that apply to an exposed/affected asset and have a threat-monitoring requirement. Where several CVEs share equivalent collection, choose one sensor rule implementation rather than installing identical candidates together. Auditing **does not remediate** a CVE: vendor patches or mitigations remain the primary response. Splunk searches may require audit-key adaptation.
- PHP2Shell files intentionally contain **commented service-binary selectors** pending installed-package/workload confirmation; do not treat them as enabled sensors merely because the file exists. These are workload-specific auditd rules; select only for relevant web/application services.
- Added `29-system-config-integrity.rules` as an **inactive Tier 2 proposal** for **write/attribute activity under `/etc`**. If promoted and enabled, it would cover creation of `/etc/ld.so.preload`, shell system profiles, SSH/sudoers and other CVE-agnostic security configuration, even when an individual target file is missing at startup. This would be a broad directory rule: it is **commented out pending collection-volume and duplicate-overlap review** and must not be described as deployed Tier 2 coverage.
- Magic SysRq procfs watches are **conditional candidates**, not active defaults, because presence and behavior vary by kernel/image. Per-user shell startup hunting and sudoers **read** monitoring remain Tier 3 candidates requiring workload scoping; no fleet-wide home read watches were added.
- **CVE-2026-111497** is a Brotli decoder vulnerability, **not** Dirty Frag; it has no fabricated auditd kernel-splice rules in this release.

## v0.14 offline package and path verification (no running host required)

This release also checks published Ubuntu generic cloud-image manifests and Amazon Linux standard/minimal AMI package comparisons. The cited generic Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 cloud images do not list `auditd` or `acl`; AL2023/AL2027 minimal AMIs do not list SSM Agent.

This release adds vendor-package evidence and explicit prerequisites for Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04, Debian 12/13, and cloud guest-agent paths. Ubuntu 26.04 `apparmor_parser` watches now target the `/usr/sbin` packaged location. Ubuntu 24.04 STIG-derived rule lines, including `/var/log/sudo.log` and `/sbin/unix_update`, are **unchanged**: each is now annotated with the necessary image/path prerequisite; the former may not exist by default and will block direct loading. GCP host files add **conditional** `.template` and guest-agent plugin-state watches. Provider-specific conditional watches are not assumed installed.

**This is not a universal no-touch drop-in.** A distribution's package manifest identifies the path shipped by a package, *not* whether that package or a dynamically-created file is present in any given cloud/golden image. The 80 variants remain engineering candidates, not production-approved or STIG-certified. See the existing guides for the offline acceptance gate and required customer applicability/exception decisions.

## v0.14 — Ubuntu 22.04/26.04 and Debian baseline remediation

- **Ubuntu 22.04 (8 architecture/hosting variants):** Expanded Tier 1 from the comprehensive Ubuntu 24.04 *audit objectives* (account management, privilege binaries, access failures, kernel modules, login records, sudoers, journald, cron), and ACTIVATED `/sbin/apparmor_parser` under V2R10 **UBTU-22-654010 / V-260604**. Retained separate `-e 2` in Finalize (**V-288816**). **Do not claim 49/49 verified V-ID coverage:** the user's SHA256 `2229b5be…` source archive was described but not supplied to this run, and a full machine-readable XCCDF audit extraction was not available for an exact rule-by-rule comparison.
- **Ubuntu 26.04 (8 variants):** Now inherits the full Ubuntu 24.04 Tier 1 engineering objectives, with native Ubuntu 26.04 `/usr/sbin/apparmor_parser`. This is **not** a published 26.04 STIG mapping; inherited rules contain optional-path prerequisites and require native 26.04 image inspection.
- **Debian 12/13 (8 variants):** Added account-admin and privileged binary execution, session/logon record watches, root xattr auditing, and denied-file access expansion. Package-dependent `sudo`, `cron`, `acl`, SSH, PAM helper, and AppArmor watches remain **conditional** so a minimal install is not guaranteed to load them. These are **Debian enterprise objectives**, not a Ubuntu product STIG certification.
- **Proxmox VE:** Debian profile is a starting point, not drop-in proof. Use supported platform/API/task/cluster logging as companion evidence; do not install the Ubuntu 24.04 STIG as if it applies to Debian.
- The remaining OS profiles, all Tier 2 rules, Tier 3 and cloud-host rules are unchanged in active semantics. **No profile is production-approved.**

**Offline prerequisites:** Presence of an executable in a vendor repository is not evidence it is installed on the deployed image. `/var/log/sudo.log`, `/var/log/faillog`, `/var/log/journal`, `/var/spool/cron` and optional utilities may be absent. Resolve via approved image prerequisites or documented exception before loading the package.

## What is in the package

- 40 OS/hosting-environment combinations: on-premises, AWS, Azure and GCP.
- **Two mutually exclusive architecture choices per OS/environment:** existing profile root is **x86_64**; its nested `aarch64/` subtree is **ARM64**. A total of **80 architecture-selectable implementations**, 25 `.rules` files each (2,000 `.rules` files).
- Four guides under `docs/` (01–04), plus this README, `AGENTS.md`, and the rule files. The repository contains no deployment script, generated combined ruleset, or automation; the flat-file distribution tools are separate delivery artifacts.
- **Tier 1 + Tier 2 mandatory** under the enterprise Minimum Security Requirement (MSR), Tier 3 as threat-directed, Finalize last.

## Choose the exact rule directory

```text
rules/
  on-prem/<os-version>/                  # x86_64
  on-prem/<os-version>/aarch64/          # ARM64
  aws/<os-version>/                      # x86_64
  aws/<os-version>/aarch64/              # ARM64
  azure/<os-version>/                    # x86_64
  azure/<os-version>/aarch64/            # ARM64
  gcp/<os-version>/                      # x86_64
  gcp/<os-version>/aarch64/              # ARM64
```

In each selected directory (at either architecture level):

```text
tier-1-baseline/        00-foundation; 10-14 OS/compliance; 18-failure-control
tier-2-core-security/   20-28 SOC/IR; 29 active /etc and shell-startup integrity
tier-3-threat-specific/ 30-exploitation + individually selected CVE-YYYY-NNNN.rules
finalize/               99-finalize.rules (-e 2; last)
```

**DO NOT** copy both the root and `aarch64/` rules, recursively install the parent profile, or combine multiple OS/environment profiles. Copy only the tier directories for the selected architecture to the host's audit rule directory after validation.

## Changes inherited from v0.12 and v0.13 (relative to v0.11)

1. **ARM64:** Added a complete `aarch64/` subprofile for every listed OS/cloud profile; translated unsupported legacy x86 syscall names to native ARM64 `*at` / `*at2` equivalents where appropriate and removed x86-only b32 rules. Architecture mapping is tested against the Linux Audit syscall-name library, *not* against every guest kernel.
2. **Execution:** Added explicit `execveat` coverage for interactive and root execution, and privilege-transition coverage. Added x86_64 b32 counterparts to additional syscall telemetry for hosts supporting the compatibility ABI.
3. **Ubuntu 24.04:** Preserved the 64 exact source directives from the user-supplied Ubuntu 24.04 V1R7 extraction on each x86_64 profile; ARM64 is a *translated engineering candidate*, not an exact DISA x86 fix-text match.
4. **RHEL 9:** Added the 81 source directives from the previously assembled **RHEL 9 V2R10 reference package**, including missing privileged command, permissions, identity, module, and cron coverage, with per-line reference comments. The older local reference is **not independently verified against the latest authoritative DISA release** and contains paths requiring image-specific prerequisites.
5. **Other systems:** Added enterprise baseline changes for audit/PAM files, identity resolution, modern access/deletion/permission syscalls, and mount/group privilege operations. These are not substitutes for product-specific STIG mapping.
6. **Cloud guests:** Added active auditing of root daemon execution (`execve`/`execveat`), daemon outbound connection attempts, and noninteractive root `/etc` changes. Provider-specific SSM/waagent/Google guest-agent/CLI/credential watches remain **explicit conditional requirements**, since a hard-coded watch against a missing file can fail to load. Exact cloud API operations **require cloud-native logs**.
7. **Documentation:** Updated deployment, architecture selection, live validation, cloud logging, risk/waiver decisions and source maintenance. All user-supplied v0.11 files remain the baseline for this revision.

Added source-linked conditional candidates for `modprobe`, `kmod`, `fdisk`, cron directories, persistent journal, and sudo file logging. The existing sudo, SSH, ACL, PAM and AppArmor candidates remain conditional on installed packages. **Do not claim active Ubuntu-rule parity:** absent files and optional packages can prevent audit rules from loading.

These are source **traceability references**, not an independently verified full DISA XCCDF check/fix equivalence assessment.

## Security and operational gates — not resolved by static tests

- **STIG completeness:** Ubuntu 24.04 has review-derived x86_64 source-line reconciliation; Ubuntu 22.04 has 49/49 V2R10 audit-rule V-IDs mapped against publicly readable check/fix text, but not independently hash-verified against the official DISA archive or host-tested; RHEL 9 has a prior local reference (81/81). Other OS versions require current product-specific DISA STIG/SRG checks, file/path applicability, and V-ID-level evidence. **No profile can be represented as fully STIG-validated.**
- **Missing paths:** `auditctl`/`augenrules` can reject `-w`, `path=`, and `dir=` watches if referenced files/directories are absent. The Ubuntu and RHEL 9 source-based candidates in particular contain required-path watches that may be absent on minimal images. Validate and resolve through prerequisite installation, approved N/A, or exception **before loading**.
- **Cloud guest agents:** Mandatory provider-specific agent/credential/CLI monitoring is conditional on what is installed. The generic root daemon rules are **not** equivalent to exact agent configuration watches. An applicable but inactive agent watch needs remediation or an approved exception.
- **Cloud control plane:** CloudTrail (AWS), Azure Activity Log (Azure), and Cloud Audit Logs (GCP) are mandatory companion sources for security-group/NSG/firewall, role/IAM, and API changes. `auditd` cannot record remote management-plane operations directly.
- **Live tests:** None of these 80 architecture-specific candidates was kernel-loaded, end-to-end event-tested, performance-tested, or Splunk-validated as part of offline packaging.
- **Availability:** `-D` clears existing audit rules; `-f 2` may panic on critical audit failure; `-e 2` makes rules immutable until reboot. Assess with the appropriate authority before any production deployment.
- **Volume:** Tier 2 `execve`, `execveat`, filesystem changes, `connect`, and daemon network monitoring can be expensive. Performance failures require remediation/tuning within the required security objective or an approved waiver.

See `docs/01-IMPLEMENTATION-GUIDE.md` for safe selection/staging, `docs/02-MINIMUM-SECURITY-REQUIREMENT-AND-WAIVER.md` for exceptions, and `docs/03-RULE-SOURCING-AND-MAINTENANCE.md` for official sources and refresh instructions.

## 10. Carry-forward work queue (not authorization to implement)

The following work remains open. This summary mirrors **AGENTS.md §10**; it does not authorize changes to mandatory rules or expand Tier 3 by itself.

1. **Tier 2 directory-integrity validation:** Assess active recursive `/etc` write/attribute monitoring for coverage across mount points, overlap with targeted watches, event volume, and audit backlog. Direct Magic SysRq procfs auditing remains conditional and unverified.
2. **Tier 3 non-CVE hunts:** Evaluate user shell initialization changes, sudoers read access, and service-scoped investigations separately. Do not promote a hunt to mandatory Tier 2 solely because a Splunk analytic uses it.
3. **CVE-specific rule applicability:** Recheck CVE references, affected OS/kernel versions, overlapping telemetry, and the currently inactive PHP2Shell executable selectors. Preserve the distinct `CVE-YYYY-NNNN.rules` files.
4. **OS-specific STIG and path verification:** Continue authoritative Ubuntu 22.04 V2R10 reconciliation and platform-specific mapping for RHEL, AlmaLinux, Oracle Linux, SUSE, Amazon Linux, and other supported profiles. Validate package/image path prerequisites and conditional cloud agents without claiming host testing or compliance.
5. **Release traceability:** Keep rule architecture/version headers, README, `AGENTS.md`, and all four guide titles synchronized in subsequent releases.

For detailed AI maintenance instructions and the current policy decisions, see `AGENTS.md`. All profiles remain **engineering candidates** until applicable validation gates are satisfied.

# 01 — Implementation Guide | v0.19

**Rule reference (repository update):** `docs/04-TIER-2-AND-3-RULE-REFERENCE.md` explains the purposes of Tier 2 and Tier 3 rule files. The examples are descriptive, not a substitute for the selected OS/cloud/architecture `.rules` directives, applicable STIG, package-path preflight, or waiver requirements.

## v0.17 — Targeted mandatory Tier 2 shell-startup monitoring

`29-system-config-integrity.rules` now includes **active** watch rules for `/etc/profile` and the OS-family Bash startup configuration (`/etc/bashrc` on RPM-family/Amazon, `/etc/bash.bashrc` on Ubuntu/Debian/SLES). On non-Debian profiles it also monitors `/etc/profile.d` (including new files within the watched subtree). These watch `wa` access, not reads or command contents. Both b64 and b32 are present on x86_64; ARM64 has b64 only.

**Deployment preflight:** Confirm that active paths exist as the expected file or directory on the selected OS/image before deploying. Package-file lists establish normal installed paths, not runtime guarantees. Debian does **not** have an automatically enabled `/etc/profile.d` watch; uncomment it only if the directory exists *and* `/etc/profile` sources it. If any applicable mandatory path is absent, remediate image prerequisites or obtain the correct applicability/exception decision; never silently disregard the rule.

**Current v0.19 boundary:** Active `/etc` directory auditing is present for file creation and modification. For host creation detection, rely on the approved native auditd parent-directory rule, assess filesystem/mount limitations, and use the waiver process if the required rule cannot be supported. SSH/sudoers watches may already exist in Tier 1; keep that provenance and only enable missing package-dependent watches when their paths exist. SysRq and user-home startup hunting remain separate/conditional. No host evidence exists for this release.


## v0.16.4 — Ubuntu 22.04 STIG coverage boundary

**Ubuntu 22.04 V2R10 (v0.16.4 offline mapping):** All **49 published audit-rule-related V-IDs** are represented by active Tier 1/Finalize directives in all eight Ubuntu 22.04 variants, including the AppArmor parser, cron watches, useradd and immutability. This is a source-to-rule presence/intent cross-check, **not** official DISA ZIP hash verification, host-load evidence, or overall STIG compliance. Mandatory watches with missing-file/package prerequisites still require remediation or an approved exception. See the full 49-row traceability table in Document 03.

## Scope and deployment decision

This package provides Linux Audit engineering candidates for **full OS hosts and VMs**, on-premises and in AWS, Azure, and GCP. It is not an auditd configuration for container-only workloads or a substitute for hypervisor/cloud audit services. Select by **actual host OS/version, hosting environment, and CPU architecture**. It does not automatically satisfy STIG configuration requirements outside audit rules.

Mandatory **Tier 1 Baseline + Tier 2 SOC/IR**; Tier 3 only when threat-directed. The finalizer (`-e 2`) is deployed *last* after validation. Obtain authorization for `-D`, `-f 2`, and `-e 2` impacts.

### 1. Select the correct directory

```bash
cat /etc/os-release
uname -m
sudo auditctl -s
```

| Host | Selected profile path (within the extracted package) |
|---|---|
| RHEL 9 x86_64 on-prem | `rules/on-prem/rhel9/` |
| RHEL 9 ARM64 on-prem | `rules/on-prem/rhel9/aarch64/` |
| Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 on AWS | `rules/aws/ubuntu2404/` |
| Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 on AWS | `rules/aws/ubuntu2404/aarch64/` |
| Amazon Linux 2023 ARM64 | `rules/aws/amazon-linux-2023/aarch64/` |
| Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64 on GCP | `rules/gcp/ubuntu2604/` |

**Never recursively copy the OS directory:** its nested `aarch64/` holds a *different, mutually exclusive* complete ruleset. For x86_64 use the profile root's immediate tier directories; for ARM64 use its `aarch64/` tier directories.

On x86_64, `arch=b64` and `arch=b32` denote separate syscall tables; b32 monitoring is included even though many images do not ship 32-bit userspace. On ARM64 only native `arch=b64` rules are installed. The ARM64 translations replace legacy syscalls absent on that ABI (for example `unlink` → `unlinkat`, `rename` → `renameat`/`renameat2`, `creat` → `openat`/`openat2`). **These mappings must be tested on the target kernel**: architecture translation is not automatically equivalent to the current OS product STIG.


### Offline, package-manifest-first path verification (v0.14)

Use a per-image assumption ledger when actual hosts are unavailable. First, confirm the exact OS/version/architecture and target image family. Next, compare each active file/directory/executable path with the **OS release's published package file lists** and cloud agent documentation. Record separately: (a) vendor-documented package location, (b) whether the package is part of the **published base image**, (c) whether the watched object is created only at boot or after configuration, (d) whether the path is a symlink/`usr-merge` alias, and (e) whether the rule will reject a missing path. A valid pathname alone is not proof of installed-file existence.

| Path or behavior | Offline conclusion and required action |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 AppArmor parser | `apparmor` manifest ships `/sbin/apparmor_parser`; do not apply 26.04 pathname to these STIG-derived rules |
| Ubuntu 26.04 AppArmor parser | `apparmor` manifest ships `/usr/sbin/apparmor_parser` (amd64/arm64); this release corrected the active rule |
| Ubuntu 24.04 PAM helpers | `libpam-modules-bin` manifest lists `/usr/sbin/{pam_timestamp_check,unix_update,unix_chkpwd}`; preserve STIG `/sbin/unix_update` only when the alias resolves to the actual inode |
| Ubuntu 24.04 `/usr/bin/chacl` | Shipped by the optional `acl` package; absence needs package remediation or applicability decision, not a silent deletion |
| Ubuntu 24.04 `/var/log/sudo.log` | Not a default sudo file log. STIG-derived watch retained; configure/create the log as approved before applying it, or document the approved exception. Missing file can reject the rule |
| `/etc/security/opasswd`, `/var/log/faillog`, login history files | Generated/legacy/conditional; published package paths alone do not establish existence |
| Debian 12 vs 13 PAM | `libpam-modules-bin` file lists differ (`/sbin` vs `/usr/sbin` helpers); review legacy aliases on Debian 12 and new paths on 13 |
| AWS SSM on Ubuntu | Snap may package under `/snap/amazon-ssm-agent/current`, with writable overrides under `/etc/amazon/ssm`; 26.04 defaults not established by cited Snap guide |
| Azure | `/etc/waagent.conf` is documented; whether the guest agent or cloud-init owns provisioning is image-specific |
| GCP | `/etc/default/instance_configs.cfg.template` overrides `.distro` and base `.cfg`; `/var/lib/google-guest-agent` holds plugin state for modern versions, and may be absent |


### Published base-image package manifests (no VM boot needed)

Official generic Ubuntu cloud-image manifests for Jammy 22.04, Noble 24.04 and Resolute 26.04 provide exact *package names* installed on a particular image build. This is stronger evidence than a distribution's package catalog, but a vendor-customized EC2/Azure/GCP image may differ. The referenced **generic Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 amd64 cloud images list `apparmor` and `libpam-modules-bin`, but not `auditd` or `acl`**. The package manager may support `auditd` without that package being preinstalled. If `acl` is absent, a STIG-derived `chacl` watch will not load; install the package or record the approved applicability exception. The `apparmor` package location can be valid without the audit subsystem being installed.

- Ubuntu 22.04 generic amd64 image: https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/jammy/current/jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.manifest
- Ubuntu 24.04 generic amd64 image: https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/noble/current/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.manifest
- Ubuntu 26.04 generic amd64 and arm64 images: https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/resolute/current/resolute-server-cloudimg-amd64.manifest and https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/resolute/current/resolute-server-cloudimg-arm64.manifest
- Amazon Linux 2023 standard/minimal/container comparison: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/linux/al2023/ug/image-comparison.html
- Amazon Linux 2027 preview standard/minimal/container comparison: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/linux/al2027/ug/AMI-minimal-and-standard-differences.html

AWS documents SSM Agent in the **standard** Amazon Linux 2023 and 2027 AMIs, **not** the minimal AMIs; `awscli-2` appears in both standard and minimal image tables, and the `audit` package is listed for those image types. Therefore *Amazon Linux version alone is insufficient to decide SSM applicability*: record whether the image is standard or minimal. AL2027 is preview-only. For Ubuntu AWS images, do not equate the generic Canonical image manifest to an EC2-specific pre-installed Snap package set.

This image-manifest evidence is suitable for an offline build prerequisite checklist. It cannot prove `/var/log/sudo.log` or `/etc/security/opasswd` exists, because such files are runtime/configuration-created and may not appear in package manifests.

**Release block:** If a mandatory audit watch targets an absent object, the profile is not a safe universal drop-in. An offline verifier cannot waive the rule on a customer's behalf. Require the image builder to create/install the prerequisite or obtain an approved applicability/waiver decision. Never call an unverified profile 'deployable' simply because it parses correctly.

### 2. Perform a path and applicability preflight

The selected directory must contain **25 `.rules` files**, distributed across the 4 tier folders. Before copying rules, check every active `-w`, `-F path=`, and `-F dir=` target against the actual host. The following is a read-only command run from the extracted package directory:

```bash
# Edit to match the exact host. For ARM64 append /aarch64 to the value.
PROFILE="$PWD/rules/aws/ubuntu2404"

awk '
  /^-w / { print $2 }
  /^-a / {
    for (i=1; i<=NF; i++)
      if ($i == "-F" && $(i+1) ~ /^(path|dir)=/) {
        split($(i+1), part, "="); print part[2]
      }
  }
' "$PROFILE"/tier-1-baseline/*.rules "$PROFILE"/tier-2-core-security/*.rules \
  | sort -u | while IFS= read -r target; do
      test -e "$target" || printf 'MISSING: %s\n' "$target"
    done
```

Resolve all `MISSING` paths: verify the exact package/service prerequisite and correct vendor path; install required components if applicable; or obtain documented **N/A or approved waiver** when not applicable. Never silently remove a mandatory rule. This is especially important for STIG execution watches and login files on Ubuntu 24.04, RHEL 9 privileged utilities, optional SELinux/AppArmor executables, and minimal cloud images. Also inspect `auditctl -l` for any preexisting `-a never,task` rule.

**MAC enforcement is separate:** run `getenforce`/`sestatus` where SELinux is installed, or `aa-status` where AppArmor is installed. Native SELinux AVC and AppArmor denial records must reach audit/journald and Splunk; watching policy edits does not capture or enable every denial.

### 3. Stage mandatory tiers (do not install finalization during tests)

Use a disposable VM/cloud instance for first testing. This procedure must be reviewed for the host's existing audit rules because **`00-audit-foundation.rules` includes `-D`**. Do not delete unrelated pre-existing audit rules without an approved change.

```bash
# Example: local staging, after resolving preflight failures.
PROFILE="$PWD/rules/aws/ubuntu2404"

sudo mkdir -p /etc/audit/rules.d
# Back up the existing audit configuration in the approved change procedure.
# Then COPY ONLY THE RULES FROM THE SELECTED PROFILE/TIERS (not recursively).
sudo install -m 0640 "$PROFILE"/tier-1-baseline/*.rules /etc/audit/rules.d/
sudo install -m 0640 "$PROFILE"/tier-2-core-security/*.rules /etc/audit/rules.d/
# Do not copy 99-finalize.rules at this point.
sudo augenrules --check
sudo augenrules --load
sudo auditctl -s
sudo auditctl -l
```

Staging is safe only if there is no preexisting `-e 2` immutable rule and the host/auditing authority approved the test. Confirm that *every intended active rule* was loaded; `augenrules --load` returning zero is insufficient evidence. Preserve terminal/kernel journal output and account for any missing watches. `-f 2` can cause a kernel panic on serious audit failure; test failure/backlog behavior in a disposable environment first. Some deployments require an authorized reboot before a changed configuration can take effect.

**Tier 3:** install only a threat-directed file with a designated owner and review date. **Finalize:** after full approval, install `finalize/99-finalize.rules`, re-check/load, and document that audit rules become immutable until reboot:

```bash
sudo install -m 0640 "$PROFILE"/finalize/99-finalize.rules /etc/audit/rules.d/
sudo augenrules --check
sudo augenrules --load
sudo auditctl -s
```

Do not apply a new profile's rules on top of a prior profile, or mix x86_64 and ARM64 files. The package deliberately does not include a deployment tool or modify host files automatically.

### 4. Validate event generation and Splunk ingestion

Generate authorized, non-destructive test events and verify corresponding audit keys/records with `ausearch -k <key> -i` or SIEM queries. At minimum test: account metadata change, sudo/privileged exec, `execve` **and `execveat`**, failed file access (`EACCES` and `EPERM`), file rename/delete, service persistence, package repo config, MAC policy administration, and (in cloud) noninteractive daemon execution/configuration change. A rule matching on a console may still fail to forward or extract relevant metadata in Splunk.

Capture before/after `auditctl -s`: `lost`, `backlog`, `backlog_limit`, and `enabled`. Validate identity correlation (`auid`, UID/EUID), `exe`, process ID, command arguments, file PATH records, event time, and source host in SIEM. Match event retention and collection routing to your enterprise policy.

**Performance gate:** lab → canary → peak load → broader deployment; compare audit loss (must not increase), sustained backlog, EPS/GB/day, CPU/system CPU, disk I/O, application SLOs, and SIEM license/retention. Mandatory Tier 2 includes broad `execve`, `execveat`, root-file-mutation and network `connect` rules. New cloud daemon rules add background execution and connection telemetry. If the workload cannot sustain a required capability, optimize without losing it or obtain an authorized waiver; do not mark it compliant.

### 5. Cloud host auditing vs cloud control-plane logs

`27-cloud-host-security.rules` activates **noninteractive root daemon** `execve`/`execveat`, `connect` and `/etc` write/attribute monitoring on the selected provider. Those events help attribute guest-management execution; they do **not** identify the AWS/Azure/GCP API call or console principal when a remote actor changes a security group, NSG, IAM policy, or firewall.

The same file includes **commented conditional provider watches**. Each image must inventory installed guest agents, CLI tools, credential/configuration directories, and enable the correct exact-path watches after the preflight. If the agent exists and the requirement applies, leaving the watch commented requires remediation or a waiver. Missing/optional agent paths are not automatically activated because `auditctl` can reject watches against missing targets.

| Provider | Verify the guest paths/components | Mandatory companion telemetry (outside auditd) |
|---|---|---|
| **AWS** | SSM Agent (`/var/lib/amazon/ssm`, `/etc/amazon/ssm`), cloud-init, AWS CLI, local AWS credential files where present | **CloudTrail** management events for EC2 security groups, IAM/STS, API calls; VPC Flow Logs and AWS Config as required |
| **Azure** | Azure Linux Agent (`/etc/waagent.conf`, `/var/lib/waagent`), cloud-init, Azure CLI and credential paths | **Azure Activity Log** for resource-manager NSG/RBAC changes; relevant identity/data/resource logs; VNet Flow Logs as applicable |
| **GCP** | Guest agent (`/etc/default/instance_configs.cfg` and variants), cloud-init, Google Cloud CLI and local credentials | **Cloud Audit Logs** (Admin Activity and relevant Data Access/Policy Denied), firewall/IAM management; VPC Flow Logs as applicable |

Ensure management events are actually enabled/collected at the required AWS account / Azure subscription / GCP project or organization scope, forwarded to SIEM, and searchable. A single guest process executing a CLI is *not* evidence that all API calls are observed by host auditd; SDK requests and control-plane calls from elsewhere are invisible to guest auditd.

### 6. Special product status

- **Ubuntu 24.04:** x86_64 Tier 1 retains 64/64 exact audit directive lines in the user-provided **V1R7 extraction** (49 rule-bearing V-IDs including `-e 2`). This is only source-line matching, **not** independent official archive verification or host STIG compliance. ARM64 translation needs its own compliance applicability review.
- **RHEL 9:** x86_64 Tier 1 includes 81/81 directives from the **prior locally assembled RHEL9 V2R10 reference package**. Each source line has a reference marker. Obtain the **current** official DISA source and independently verify V-IDs, N/A conditions, paths, and behavior. ARM64 translation is not certified by the old reference.
- **Other OS versions:** not yet mapped to their current, respective product-specific STIG/SRG. Shared enterprise coverage rules are intentionally **not** evidence of equivalent compliance. Do not transfer another product's STIG V-ID to them.
- **Ubuntu 26.04:** AppArmor 5.x and cloud agents require live validation. No current Ubuntu 26.04 product STIG has been independently verified here; apply the authorized SRG/organizational baseline until one is available.
- **Amazon Linux 2027:** treat as preview-only; no production approval or STIG claim.

### 7. Release evidence for each deployment

Record OS release, architecture, provider/account/project, image ID/kernel/audit version, applicable STIG release, enabled modules/agents, preflight path results, rule-load output, executed test cases, Splunk events/field extraction, audit loss/backlog/EPS, peak performance, cloud-native feed coverage, applicable N/A/waiver ticket, approval, and expiry/retest date. Only promote an individual **OS + cloud + architecture + tested image/kernel** after all gates pass.

## v0.14 — Deployment and applicability: Ubuntu and Debian gaps

**N1 (Ubuntu 22.04 V2R10; historical v0.14 assessment, superseded by the v0.16.4 published-source mapping above):** The former sparse profile was replaced with a broader Tier 1 candidate reflecting the Ubuntu 24.04 audit objectives but with Ubuntu 22.04 specific AppArmor parser activation (`/sbin/apparmor_parser`, V-260604). V2R10 immutability (V-288816) remains in Finalize. Obtain and preserve the original official V2R10 archive SHA256 (review references `2229b5be…` but that archive was not included in this task), extract the full audit rule-bearing V-IDs, compare all check/fix requirements, and document remaining differences. **Do not state full 49/49 verified STIG coverage.**

**N2 (Ubuntu 26.04):** The Tier 1 directives now match the Ubuntu 24.04 *engineering objectives* except for release-specific AppArmor handling and documented prerequisite assumptions. They must **not** be labeled an Ubuntu 26.04 DISA STIG baseline. Assess the exact current vendor package/image manifests and do not silently ignore missing watches.

**N3 (Debian 12/13 and Proxmox):** Added explicit user/privileged-command monitoring, login-record watches, and file-access objectives using Debian-specific path assumptions. Commands from packages not universally present (`sudo`, `acl`, PAM helpers, `openssh-client`, `cron`, AppArmor) remain commented as **conditional** requirements pending package installation or verified applicability, not automatically N/A. For Proxmox, `/etc/pve` is a `pmxcfs` FUSE filesystem; do not presume that ordinary auditd watch semantics cover its clustered configuration. Pair host audit with supported Proxmox task/API/cluster log sources.

**Acceptance rule:** These changes improve *engineering coverage* and remove the misleading parity assumption; they do not substitute for source V-ID reconciliation, image-path checks, kernel loading, event evidence or the organizational waiver process.

## v0.15 — Debian 12/13 and Proxmox preflight (without host event collection)

The Debian Tier 1 audit objective is mandatory, but no **unconditional** file watch can be promised to load against every Debian/Proxmox image. In particular, do not copy Ubuntu `-w /var/log/journal`, `/var/log/sudo.log`, legacy lastlog/faillog, `cron`, `sudo`, `acl`, or AppArmor paths without their installed-file prerequisites. Auditd may reject a watch if its target does not exist. An uncommented watch is not an installation step.

For a managed Debian or PVE image, verify package ownership and default paths against Debian 12 (Bookworm) / Debian 13 (Trixie) package inventories before enabling conditional rules. Typical validation commands **on a representative image or image filesystem** (not event-log testing) are:

```bash
dpkg-query -W sudo cron openssh-client libpam-modules-bin acl apparmor kmod fdisk auditd
dpkg-query -L sudo openssh-client libpam-modules-bin apparmor kmod fdisk | grep -E '(sudoedit|ssh-agent|ssh-keysign|pam_timestamp_check|apparmor_parser|modprobe|/kmod$|/fdisk$)'
for p in /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d /etc/cron.d /var/spool/cron /var/log/journal /var/log/sudo.log /var/log/lastlog /var/log/faillog /run/utmp /etc/security/opasswd; do test -e "$p" && echo "PRESENT $p" || echo "ABSENT $p"; done
```

If package/image access is unavailable, retain conditional rules as **unverified and not satisfied**, not N/A. Obtain approval for prerequisite installation or a documented exception. For Proxmox, do not assume that a local audit watch on `pmxcfs` (`/etc/pve`) captures all clustered changes; obtain supported Proxmox API/task/cluster telemetry. PVE 8 is out of vendor support; prioritize PVE 9/Debian 13.


## v0.16 — Selecting CVE and hunting rules

**Mandatory baseline (v0.19):** Install Tier 1 and all applicable Tier 2 rules. `29-system-config-integrity.rules` retains v0.17 targeted shell-startup watches and now adds an active recursive `/etc` write/attribute watch; confirm overlap, volume, and availability risk. An authorized waiver is required if the mandatory monitoring cannot be supported.

**CVE actions:** Confirm OS/package/kernel susceptibility using the relevant vendor advisory, then **patch or apply an approved mitigation**. If exposure persists or threat monitoring is required, select the matching `CVE-YYYY-NNNN.rules` from Tier 3; this **detects selected behavior only** and is not an effective substitute for patching. Do not copy all `CVE-*.rules` by wildcard. Copies of matching rules across two CVE files are intentional for individual selection, **not** authorization to load every copy. If multiple CVEs require identical rules, install one equivalent set and document both CVE requirements; account for overlapping keys and SPL filters. Rule keys such as `af_alg`, `splice_user` and `process_creation` must match the selected detection or be translated in SPL.

**PHP2Shell caveat:** `CVE-2026-109618.rules` and `CVE-2026-109619.rules` contain commented candidate `exe=` filters. Select and uncomment a candidate only if the exact web/application-server executable is installed and relevant to the workload. No default enabled syscall rule exists for this CVE family because blanket service-account execution collection could be excessive. These CVE-named files do not assume an additional endpoint product; their workload selectors must be explicitly configured for the applicable service. Both PHP CVE files implement the same process sensor; pick one when both apply.

**Ordering:** Stage selected CVE files and any approved conditional rule edits **before** installing finalization with `-e 2`; later activation/retirement of rules on an immutable host normally requires reboot/redeployment of the audit ruleset. Do not treat a duplicate add failure as evidence the kernel chose a valid preferred rule. Check the effective rule set and audit keys during deployment.

**CVE-independent hunting:** Monitoring every user's `.bashrc` or `.profile`, and sudoers read access, remains a targeted Tier 3/hunting decision, not a mandatory Tier 2 change. The SysRq procfs candidates in `29-system-config-integrity.rules` are also conditional until the kernel/image supports them.

## v0.19: Auditd-only Tier 2 configuration integrity

**Approved rule:** Every selected OS/architecture profile now contains active `-F dir=/etc -F perm=wa -k t2_etc_integrity` rules in `29-system-config-integrity.rules`. x86_64 uses both b64 and b32; ARM64 uses native b64. This does not rely on any non-auditd endpoint software.

1. **Loader-preload first creation:** A single-file watch cannot cover a file that is absent at rule load. The recursive `/etc` watch captures writes, creations, renames, and metadata changes under the directory when supported by the kernel/filesystem. Investigate `PATH` records for the precise target, including the loader preload configuration. This may not capture modifications in separate mount points or nonstandard loader paths; assess those separately.
2. **SSH and sudoers:** This new baseline provides auditd write/attribute visibility to `/etc/ssh`, `/etc/sudoers`, and `/etc/sudoers.d`, including file creation, *whether or not* optional packages are present at rule load time. Pre-existing targeted rules remain, even when they overlap, to preserve source mappings and audit keys; only enable additional commented exact-path watches when a path exists and has a documented need.
3. **Magic SysRq:** Persistent changes in `/etc/sysctl.conf` and `/etc/sysctl.d/` fall under the new `/etc` watch. They do **not** prove detection of a direct privileged write to `/proc/sysrq-trigger` or `/proc/sys/kernel/sysrq`. Procfs candidates remain commented pending verified kernel acceptance. An absence of SysRq events cannot be counted as successful monitoring; document that runtime limitation and seek an approved waiver if it is mandatory for the host.
4. **Collection cost:** A recursive watch is wider than the targeted rules it supplements. Before customer rollout, confirm the expected event rate and loss/backlog risk in the organization's workload acceptance process. Without host access these measurements cannot be certified. Audit failure mode remains `-f 2` (kernel panic on critical audit failures), and any inability to support Tier 2 must use an authorized, scoped exception rather than deleting it silently.
5. **Audit event transport:** Preserve native `SYSCALL`, `PATH`, `CWD`, `EXECVE`, and `PROCTITLE` records, event serial IDs and audit keys, and use the `PATH` records to filter `/etc/ld.so.preload`, sudoers, SSH and SysRq configuration changes in Splunk. This is **auditd telemetry**, not a requirement for an additional host monitoring agent.
6. **Cloud boundary:** Local auditd cannot provide an authoritative record of remote cloud API calls. Cloud-host API/security-group/IAM monitoring requirements must be handled at the cloud control plane, separately from host auditd.

**Linux Audit documentation:** https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/auditctl.8.html ; https://github.com/linux-audit/audit-userspace ; **SysRq kernel documentation:** https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/sysrq.html
